articles.author: Visitor
articles.summary: West Chester, Pa. On Saturday, October 28, the corner-stone of the new A.M.E. Church was laid by Bishop Wayman at 2 o'clock; $140 was raised. A second note signed V. reports that Bishop Wayman laid the corner-stone of a new church at Media, Pa., on Friday, October 27.

articles.author: Wm. Nesbit
articles.summary: Letter dated Altoona, Pa., Oct. 26, 1865, on the organization of auxiliary leagues of the Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League in the interior of the state: Lewistown, Huntingdon, Bedford, Williamsport, Lock Haven, Bellefonte, Phillipsburg, Johnstown, Blairsville, Indiana, Hollidaysburg and Altoona.

articles.headline: Special Notice; Absence from Home
articles.author: Elisha Weaver
articles.summary: Our correspondents will please notice the following: all matter intended for this paper must be directed to Rev. Elisha Weaver or Christian Recorder; matters of books, paper or money to Box 2975 unless sent by express, when to No. 619 Pine street. The editor will be absent from home for a few weeks; private letters to be marked 'Private'.

articles.headline: A Grand Location for our Book Concern
articles.summary: We have at last succeeded in bargaining for a good house and lot, located in a business portion of our city. We want the sum of fifteen hundred dollars by the 1st of December, 1865, to enable us to effect the desired object; when paid for, we will be enabled to teach young men the art of setting type.

articles.headline: Lights and Shadows. Colored Gentlemen of Philadelphia (from the Saturday Night)
articles.summary: Clipped from the Saturday Night, a new weekly of the city. Have any Philadelphia readers seen on our streets a tall, straight, large-framed mulatto of about sixty-five who wears spectacles? It is barely possible they have seen Rev. Stephen Smith, said to be the wealthiest colored man in this section of the country.

articles.headline: Quite a Blunder; A Veteran Returning South
articles.summary: Correction to the editorial sketch of the grand parade in Baltimore (Rev. Schureman's church: 'slate roof'). Chaplain H. M. Turner, late of the 1st U.S.C.T., ordered to report for duty at Macon, Georgia, has been on a visit to our city prior to his departure for the South.

articles.headline: A New Claim Agency
articles.summary: By reference to our advertising columns, our readers will see that Rev. C. Leonard, late chaplain U.S.A., has opened a military and naval claim agency, where colored seamen and soldiers can have all claims for pay, bounty, &c., attended to. Rev. C. Leonard has collected some thousands of dollars for our soldiers, for which he received no pay.

articles.headline: What God Has Cleansed, Call Not Thou Common or Unclean (letter)
articles.author: Sea Side
articles.summary: Prompted by the speech, reported in the Philadelphia Press, of Mr. Joseph Parker, Corresponding Secretary of the American Union Commission, delivered in the church of Rev. Mr. Suydam, corner of Seventh and Spring Garden streets, saying that Pennsylvania would follow Connecticut and Alabama in refusing the negro the vote.

articles.headline: Letter from Bishop Nazrey
articles.author: W. Nazrey
articles.summary: After a long silence, I will speak again to my friends and the numerous readers of your excellent journal, which I labored with you so hard to establish. Chatham, C.W., Oct. 26th, 1865. On farming and the tilling of the soil; lists his own harvest.

articles.headline: Pennsylvania Colonization Society (from the Episcopal Recorder)
articles.summary: On Sunday evening last, the Rev. Mr. Crummel, from Liberia, delivered the annual sermon before the Pennsylvania Colonization Society, in the Church of the Epiphany. Mr. Crummel was followed by Bishop McIlvaine.

articles.headline: 'Mustering Out' (letter from the 3d U.S.C.T.)
articles.author: Wm. H. Johnson
articles.summary: Office Judge Advocate, Jacksonville, East Florida, Oct. 21, 1865. The Third Regiment has some idea of being mustered out of service; the mustering-out rolls of the Third United States Colored Troops came last evening, and you may look for us about the 20th or 30th of November. Over ninety sick.

articles.headline: Information Wanted (Richard Parker)
articles.author: Richard Parker
articles.summary: Information wanted of the whereabouts of my wife, Sophia Parker, and my two children, George Walker Parker and Mary Fanny Parker. They formerly belonged to Thomas Keyth of Culpeper County, Virginia, who moved in 1860 to Winchester, Franklin County, Tennessee. Richard Parker, 251 North 18th St., Philadelphia.

articles.headline: Marriages
articles.summary: On Oct. 19th, in Harrisburg, Pa., by Rev. Wm. H. Russell, a Harrisburg couple. On Wednesday evening, Nov. 1st, by Rev. Stephen Smith, Mr. Wm. Young to Miss Ann Harris, both of this city.

articles.headline: Obituary
articles.author: Cupid and Mary White
articles.summary: Died at Donaldsonville, La., Sept. 18, 1865, Alexander Atwood, Sergt. Co. E, 11th U.S.C.T. (of Chatham, C.W.). Departed this life September 9th, 1865, Rev. Elzey Bainard [VERIFY], a faithful minister of the A.M.E. Church, aged forty-two, a link in the chain of Woodbury Church. Died in this city on the 20th of October, Vonley Duckett [VERIFY], infant son of John W. and Isabella Page, aged nine months and thirteen days.
people: deceased Sept. 9, 1865; A.M.E. minister, Woodbury Church, aged 42 (Rev.; printed 'Rev. E. Bainard' in the text; heading given name read 'Elzey' [VERIFY])

articles.summary: Branch Agency, No. 4[?]0 Walnut St., Philadelphia, Thomas S. Malcolm, Agent. General Office, No. 402 N.Y. Avenue, Washington, D.C. Soldiers and seamen can have their claims made out at the lowest rates. C. Leonard, late Chaplain U.S.A. nov4-1m.

articles.headline: Dr. David Rosell (card)
articles.summary: Dr. David Rosell, 907 Lombard Street. Office hours / Sprech-Stunden. Oct 21-6mo. Philadelphia.

articles.headline: Colored Soldiers' and Seamen's U.S. Government Claim Office (John J. Keefe, Jr.)
articles.summary: John J. Keefe, Jr., Attorney, No. 511 S. Sixth St. (below Lombard), Philadelphia. Soldiers' and seamen's claims for U.S. bounty, state and city bounty, pensions, back pay, prize money. Oct 28-3mos.

articles.headline: The Reception of the Colored Soldiers at Harrisburg (letter)
articles.author: L'Overture
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: Please pardon my intrusion on the columns of your paper. But I could not allow the opportunity to escape of making a few remarks in the matter of the proposed reception of the colored braves of Pennsylvania. Recalls that men collecting in Lancaster county and Philadelphia to join the 55th Massachusetts remained to form the 3d U.S.C.T., the first black regiment formed on the soil of Pennsylvania; the people of Pennsylvania, under the auspices of the Garnet League of Harrisburg, propose to give a 'reception' in the capital; the invitation extends to Pennsylvanians who served in the navy; urges the first ninety men who left the city (sent home by the Governor in 1863) to take part.

articles.headline: On the March (letter)
articles.author: John H. Jones
articles.summary: When I received my appointment, last Conference, from the Rev. Bishop A. W. Wayman, and when I came to this field of labor, I began to look around, and in doing so I found that things were in a very dry and low state. First quarterly meeting July [2]3d, with the aid of Rev. A. C. Crippen; second quarter Oct. 22d (new carpet, matting and sacrament set; Rev. D. D. McClane [VERIFY], of Red Bank, preached); second quarterly meeting at Riceville, Oct. 29th. Dated Riceville [VERIFY], N.J., Oct. 30th, 1865.
people: assisted at the first quarterly meeting (Rev.)

articles.headline: A Return of Thanks (letter)
articles.author: R. F. Gibbs
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: I wish to occupy a small space in your valuable paper, as I wish to return my sincere thanks to the members and friends of the Union A.M.E. Church, Coates [VERIFY] St., Philadelphia, Pa. Soon after I entered upon my new field of labor, to which I was appointed on June 19th, 1865, I inquired of the trustees concerning the financial condition of the church, and was told that there was something like three hundred and fifty dollars, more or less, against the church. Philadelphia, Pa., Nov. 7th, 1865.
people: invited to the Oct. 29 collection (Rt. Rev.)
presented a Bible to the pastor

articles.headline: Union is Free (report)
articles.author: A Trustee
articles.summary: Through the persevering efforts of Elder R. F. Gibbs, we are enabled truthfully to say that the Union is free. This was established as a fact on last Sunday evening, by the announcement of Bishop Wayman from the pulpit that we had realized by collection through the day the sum of $616.59. This is the largest amount ever raised at any one time in the Union Church. He has only been stationed here three months and a half, having been transferred from the New York District in July.

articles.headline: Letter from Chambersburg, Pa.
articles.author: George M. Witten
articles.summary: When I received my appointment in Baltimore City, on the 24th of April, from the hand of our beloved Bishop D. A. Payne... Quarterly meetings at Chambersburg, Greencastle and Mercersburg with Rev. William Waters, presiding elder; a watch presented to the pastor by Mr. Samuel Richardson, called on Rev. Terry Hollems [VERIFY] to present it. Out of the Philadelphia area: names not linked.

articles.headline: Welcome to our Colored Soldiers (editorial)
articles.summary: The good people of Pennsylvania, ever ready to show their appreciation of every good and noble act, have, through the Garnet E. R. League, of Harrisburg, made most brilliant arrangements to tender a formal welcome to our returned heroes. This reception will occur on next Tuesday, 14th inst., at Harrisburg. Recommends the Philadelphia and Reading Rail Road.

articles.headline: Life Insurance (editorial)
articles.summary: We are pleased to note the growing tendency among our people to have some of their spare means invested in paying for a policy of insurance upon their lives. Names the Security Life Insurance Company, which has lately paid a $2000 policy on the death of one of our citizens, well-known and much respected; the agent, Mr. Willets, has his office at 528 Walnut St., above 5th.

articles.headline: Decease of an Esteemed Member of Society (Maurice Hall)
articles.summary: We are called upon to make the painful announcement of the demise of our esteemed friend and fellow-townsman, Maurice Hall. He was taken ill on the 1st instant and died on the 8th instant, at a quarter after eleven o'clock. Bethel church has lost one of her brightest Christian ornaments; Brother Hall was one of the oldest, if not the oldest, member of Bethel church. He was between 73 and 75. Thus two of the most worthy of our citizens, Joshua Brown and Maurice Hall, have left us within the short space of forty-eight hours.
people: deceased Nov. 8, 1865; one of the oldest members of Bethel church, aged between 73 and 75
deceased within forty-eight hours of Maurice Hall (c. Nov. 6-8, 1865)

articles.headline: Notice to the Itinerant Ministers of the Philadelphia Annual Conference (superannuated preachers)
articles.author: A. W. Wayman
articles.summary: Dear Brethren: Allow me to call your attention to the collections ordered by the Annual Conference, for the superannuated preachers. There are two Reverend Fathers dependent on these collections for support. Rev. Jeremiah G. Bulah [VERIFY] is nearly a hundred years of age, and is very feeble.

articles.headline: Notice of a special meeting of the Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League
articles.author: William Nesbit
articles.summary: A special meeting of the Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League will be held in Harrisburg, on Monday evening, Nov. 13th; also a public meeting on the evening of the 14th, to lay the claims of the Equal Rights movement before the people of Pennsylvania. By order of the Executive Board, William Nesbit, Pres.; Jacob C. White, Charles B. Colly, Secretaries. Philadelphia, Nov. 7th, 1865.
people: secretary, Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League (printed 'Jacob C. White', no Jr./Sr.)

articles.headline: Obituary (George R. Todd)
articles.author: F. J. C.
articles.summary: Departed this life Oct. 31st, 1865, George [VERIFY] R. Todd, in the hope of a glorious immortality, aged 36 years, 8 months and 23 days. He had been in the naval service of the United States (ship Hartford), was sent home to Philadelphia, and subsequently removed to Wilmington to his mother's. Funeral sermon by Rev. Edward Chippy and Rev. Isaac Parker in the African Union Church; interred in St. Peter's cemetery.

articles.headline: S. Shorter Hawkins, New Fall and Winter Dry Goods
articles.summary: New Fall and Winter Dry Goods. All the latest styles of merinos, alpacas, poplins, delaines, palmettas, lasnettes, fancy cloths; colored and white flannels; balmorals and hoop-skirts; gentlemen's furnishing goods. Call and see at the old stand, S. Shorter Hawkins, 615 Lombard Street, Philada.

articles.headline: Proceedings of the Annual Meeting of the Pennsylvania State Equal Rights' League, held in Harrisburg, August 9th and 10th, 1865 (continued)
articles.author: J. C. White, Jr.
articles.summary: Continued from our issue of Sept. 2d. Morning Session, August 10. The League met at 10 o'clock, Mr. President Peck in the chair. The meeting was opened by the reading of the 86th Psalm, after which the roll was called and tax collected. Includes the Report of the Executive Board (signed J. C. White, Jr., Secretary), the list of auxiliary associations, the treasurers' accounts and the resolutions.
people: Secretary, Executive Board (printed 'J. C. White, Jr.')

articles.headline: The Funeral of the Late Maurice Hall
articles.summary: The funeral of our late much lamented brother, Maurice Hall, took place on last Monday, 13th inst., from his residence, No. 1043 Lombard street at 10 o'clock, A.M. The solemn cortege formed in the following order: official members of Bethel Church, Rev. Wm. Moore, pastor of do., the invited clergy, relatives of the deceased, followed by a vast concourse of friends.
people: deceased; residence No. 1043 Lombard street; leader and steward of Bethel; leading spirit in establishing the Aged Home

articles.headline: The Harrisburg Celebration
articles.summary: The city of Harrisburg was thronged on Tuesday with hosts of visitors from all parts of the State, all desirous of expressing in a proper manner the thanks of the people to the colored soldiers. The weather was fine. At 9 o'clock the military and civic societies assembled on State street, and the line having been formed, by 10 o'clock it was in motion.
people: evening speaker at the Wesleyan Union Church (printed 'J. C. White, Jr.' = Jacob C. White Jr.)
evening speaker at the Wesleyan Union Church

articles.headline: A Voice from Ashmun
articles.author: Inveritas [VERIFY]
articles.summary: It has been some time since I have communicated to the people through your columns. I now take this opportunity of informing the many friends of Ashmun how we are progressing here. The students have organized a literary society, called the 'Garnet Lyceum,' in honor of Henry Highland Garnet. Ashmun Institute, Oxford, Pa., Nov. 11th, 1865.

articles.headline: A Revival (First Colored Wesley Church, Lombard St.)
articles.author: I. H.
articles.summary: There being such a glorious revival going on at the First Colored Wesley Church, Lombard St., among the young folks especially, I thought it would be interesting to your readers. It has been in session now for four weeks, and between eighty and ninety, during that time, have declared that Jesus has opened their eyes. The meeting is still going on under the pastoral charge of the Rev. J. P. Hemmer [VERIFY].

articles.headline: Notice: Supreme Grand Tent of J. R. Giddings and Jolliffe Union
articles.summary: To whom it may concern. To perpetuate the names of two eminent statesmen, advocates of universal freedom and the rights of mankind, the several Tents of J. R. Giddings and Jolliffe Union met in solemn convention on the 11th day of March, 1865, in the city of Philadelphia, Pa. The Grand Body was organized under the name and title of the Supreme Grand Tent of J. R. Giddings and Jolliffe Union of the United States of North America.

articles.headline: Notice to our Citizens (Wm. Henry Williams seeks his aunt)
articles.summary: If this should meet the eye of Mrs. Henrietta Williams, formerly of Macon, Ga., or of any one who knows her address, a favor will be conferred by sending the same to her nephew Wm. Henry Williams, alias Ross, care of Christian Recorder, 619 Pine street. Nov 18-2t.

articles.headline: Special Notice: Bishop Wayman's Appointments
articles.author: A. W. Wayman
articles.summary: Sunday, Nov 19th, dedication of the basement of Ebenezer Church, Baltimore; Nov. 20 Acteria [VERIFY] Creek, Md.; Nov. 21 Port Deposit; Friday Nov. 24th Chester, Pa.; Sunday 26th dedication at Morristown, N.J.; then Rahway, Elizabeth, Bergen, Riceville, Fair Haven, Gouldtown, Springtown, Bridgeton, Woodbury, Pennington, Trenton; Thursday morning, Dec 7th, at 11 o'clock, Bethel Church, Philadelphia, thanksgiving sermon. Baltimore, Nov. 9th, 1865.

articles.headline: Obituary: Bethel Official Board on Maurice Hall; deaths
articles.summary: Philada., Nov. 12th, 1865. At a called meeting of the Official Board of Bethel A.M.E. Church, Sixth St. above Lombard, the Rev. Wm. Moore, elder in charge, presiding, to take action in relation to the death of Maurice Hall, late leader and steward in this church, preamble and resolutions were submitted by Bro. articles.headline: A Visit to Wilmington, Del.
articles.author: N. H. Turpin
articles.summary: On the 15th of October last, I made a visit to Wilmington, my native place, the first time in sixteen years, to assist the Rev. D. P. Seaton with his quarterly meeting. It is astonishing to see the rapid progress the A.M.E. Church has made in that city within twenty years. Bishop A. W. Wayman preached on the fifth and left on the sixth for the City of Brotherly Love. Salem, N.J., Nov. 14th, 1865.

articles.headline: At Home (editor's return)
articles.summary: We give notice to our friends and the public that we have arrived home safe and sound, and for which we render thanks to a wise and protecting Creator. We are now ready to attend to any deferred business. We also call special attention of our Church and brethren to Bishop Payne's very interesting letter relative to the centenary.

articles.headline: Proceedings of the Annual Meeting of the Pennsylvania State Equal Rights' League, Harrisburg, Aug. 9th and 10th, 1865 (continued)
articles.summary: [Continued from our last issue.] A communication was received from the Lewistown League. Mr. Bustill of Philadelphia objected to the reading of it. Mr. Forten, of Philadelphia, moved that the rules be suspended in order to consider an important resolution concerning the Ladies' Union Association. (Carried.)

articles.headline: Semi-Centenary of the A.M. Episcopal Church
articles.author: D. A. Payne
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: The majority of your readers who are members of the A.M.E. Church seem not to be aware of the interesting fact, that the 18th of next April fills up the first half century of our existence as an ecclesiastical establishment. Central Committee: Rev. J. M. Brown, D. W. Moore, Benj. T. Tanner, M. F. Sluby, J. A. Handy, S. L. Hammonds, J. J. Herbert. Goal $100,000 for Wilberforce University, Missions and the Book Concern.

articles.headline: Death of Dr. J. McCune Smith; Bishop Campbell's Visits; Missouri and Louisiana Conference Appointments
articles.summary: With heart almost too full for utterance do we attempt to apprise those of our readers who are not already acquainted with the fact, of the death of our distinguished fellow-worker, Dr. James McCune Smith. He breathed his last on Friday, the 17th inst., at his home in Williamsburgh, N.Y. (New York; out of scope.) Bishop J. P. Campbell is returning from the Missouri and Louisiana Conferences.
people: Bishop; returning from the Missouri and Louisiana Conferences

articles.headline: Tribute of Respect: Bethel Sabbath School teachers on Maurice Hall

R. Seymour, the following preamble and resolutions were submitted and adopted: Whereas, we have learned with deep regret of the sudden demise of Maurice Hall, one of the founders of our school. Nov. 12, 1865.

articles.headline: Letter from Salem (N.J.)
articles.author: Joseph Gibbs [VERIFY]
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: Again I resume my pen to note a few of the passing events, as times are lively, and the wheel of improvement continues to move slowly in our midst. On Sabbath, the 5th inst., our hearts were made to rejoice with the presence of our highly esteemed Bishop, the Right Rev. A. W. Wayman. This is the first year Salem has been set apart as a station; N. H. Turpin is the first pastor. Hon. Wm. Steward, of Bridgeton, came en route for Trenton to meet the executive committee of the Equal Rights League of the State of New Jersey. Salem, Nov. 6th, 1865.

articles.headline: Cheating the Soldiers. A Warning.
articles.summary: We wish to call the special attention of our soldiers that are now being mustered out and paid off at Camp Cadwallader, to the fact that there are a certain party of vending Jews who frequent the locality with their wagons, for the purpose of decoying and swindling the unwary. Recommends Mr. E. Matlack & Son, 904 Market St., or Jones' one-price establishment.

articles.headline: Bishops' Meeting; Half a Centenary of the A.M.E. Church; A New Masonic Gavel; Agents
articles.summary: We are truly glad that our Bishops are going to have a meeting, about the 17th of this month. A New Masonic Gavel: a monthly paper published at Annapolis, Md., called the Masonic Gavel, devoted exclusively to the cause of Free Masonry, edited and published by a colored gentleman named John W. Reams. Agents named for New Orleans, Mobile and Natchez (out of scope).

articles.headline: Equal Rights (letter on the Philadelphia leagues)
articles.author: J. W. Brown
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: As this seems to be the time for agitation, and as our people in Philadelphia appear to be at a stand still in reference to their equal rights, I wish to make a few timely suggestions. There are in this city a number of Equal Rights' Leagues, supported by the few for the direct interest and benefit of the masses. There are meetings held time after time, and there is scarcely enough at these meetings to form a quorum.

articles.headline: Letter from Woodbury, N.J. (Freedmen's Relief Association)
articles.author: Lucy Ann Tudas [VERIFY]
articles.summary: I will commence by giving a brief account of a public demonstration, held in the A.M.E. church of this place, on the evening of the 23d inst., for the benefit of the Freedmen's Relief Association, which society was organized a few months ago, under the direction of the ladies. Address by Rev. N. H. Turpin, from Salem; $32.01 [VERIFY] realized.

articles.headline: A Donation Visit (Fair Haven, N.J.)
articles.author: M. Lee, R. Coates [VERIFY], M. Brown, Committee
articles.summary: Fair Haven, N.J., Nov. 17, 1865. We feel it our duty to return thanks to God and to the friends in general for what they have done for us. We were back with preacher's salary, and through the exertion of three sisters attached to our church, we were enabled to raise the sum of thirty-five dollars, which we shall pay to our worthy pastor, Rev. J. H. Jones.

events.name: Union A.M.E. Church debt jubilee and Sabbath collection
events.description: Reported by the pastor R. F. Gibbs (letter dated Nov. 7) and by 'A Trustee'. Gibbs, appointed June 19, 1865 (transferred from the New York District in July), found about $350 against the church and set Oct. 29 to raise $325. Elder [Wm.] Moore preached in the morning, Elder Schureman in the afternoon, and a white clergyman at night; Bishop Wayman announced $616.59 raised, the largest amount ever raised at one time in Union Church. The jubilee began Monday night [Oct. 30]: Bishop Wayman preached the jubilee sermon, followed by Elder Moore; Messrs. Wm. Davis, Fred. H. Evans (Frederick H. Evans in Gibbs's letter) and Henry Robertson presented a handsomely bound Bible to the pastor, the presentation speech by Wm. Davis. On Sunday afternoon the Sunday school presented $11; the 'Lone Star' association of young men $16 (Gibbs's letter says seventeen dollars); the young ladies' 'Fair Committee' $10. Gibbs's letter gives the church street as Coates St. [VERIFY]. The Nov. 4 issue's figure of $517.86 is superseded by $616.59 here.

events.name: Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League, special meeting and public meeting at Harrisburg (called)
events.description: Special meeting of the Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League, Monday evening Nov. 13, 1865, and a public meeting on the evening of the 14th to lay the claims of the Equal Rights movement before the people of Pennsylvania, timed with the Harrisburg reception of colored soldiers. Called by order of the Executive Board: William Nesbit, President; Jacob C. White and Charles B. Colly, Secretaries. Dated Philadelphia, Nov. 7th, 1865.

events.name: Pennsylvania State Equal Rights' League, annual meeting at Harrisburg, second day (Aug. 10, 1865): Executive Board report, auxiliary leagues, nominating committee, resolutions
events.description: Continuation of the proceedings (first part printed Sept. 2, in the database). Morning session, President [John] Peck in the chair. Rev. Theodore Green elected a corresponding member on motion of Mr. D. Williams of Hollidaysburg. Report of the Executive Board adopted on motion of Mr. Brown of Hollidaysburg: in the city of Philadelphia six auxiliary leagues formed; seventeen organizations identified with the League by payment of the representation fee; two memorials printed and sent to the State Legislature, one on equal privileges on railroad cars and the other on the elective franchise; numerous public meetings in Philadelphia; a State Convention held at Harrisburg in February; the Solicitor instructed to issue circulars to churches, lodges and other organizations; at a recent meeting of the Philadelphia members committees were appointed for the several districts to hold public meetings. AUXILIARY ASSOCIATIONS REPRESENTED: No. 1, Colored People's Union League Association of Philadelphia, four representatives, Jan. 3d, 1865, $25: John C. Bowers, Stephen Purnell [VERIFY], Jesse E. Glasgow, Rev. John H. Colbert [VERIFY]. No. 2, Equal Rights' League of Sixth District of Phila., one representative, Jan. 27th, 1865, $10: Nathaniel W. Depee. No. 3, John Brown E. R. White [VERIFY]. No. 6, Ladies' Union Association of Harrisburg: Mrs. Anna E. Amos [VERIFY], Miss Mary Williams alternate. No. 7, Reading E. R. League No. 1, Berks county: Henry B. Fry. No. 8, Friendship Lodge No. 896, G. U. O. of O. F., Phila., one representative, July 31st, 1865, $10: George Whittaker [VERIFY]; Rev. R. Fauset [VERIFY], alternate. No. 9, Lincoln E. R. League, First District of Phila., one representative, August 1st, 1865, $10: Henderson Davis, Jr. No. 10, Rising Sun E. R. League, Second District of Phila., one representative, August 8th, 1865, $10: Lorenzo D. Blackston. No. 11, New Castle E. R. League, Lawrence county: Charles W. Nighten [VERIFY]. No. 12, Benevolent E. R. League, Erie: Henry T. Busley [VERIFY]. No. 13, Bellefonte E. R. League: Franklin Johnson. No. 14, Altoona E. R. League: William Nesbit and John Alexander. No. 15, Hollidaysburg E. R. League: Daniel Williams and Moses Brown. No. 16, Huntingdon E. R. League: John G. Chaplin. No. 17, Pittsburgh E. R. League, Allegheny county: Prof. Geo. B. Vashon. Whole number of associations 17, representatives 22, alternates 4, contributed by auxiliaries $205. Exhibit 1: Dr. James H. Wilson, Treas., in account with the League (receipts $251.59; payments to Jan. 31 publishing bill Recorder $22; printing, Crummill; Solicitor; State Agent; meeting committee; A. M. Green, car case, $30; Langston committee; balance July 19 $2.19). Exhibit 2: James Needham, Treas. (from July 19; balance in fund Aug. 1 $53.50). Mr. Lorenzo D. Blackston of Philadelphia submitted rules for the government of the meetings. Mr. Bustill of Philadelphia presented a resolution on circulating the speeches of Hon. Wm. D. Kelley, Wendell Phillips and Frederick Douglass and letters of Elizur Wright and Robert Dale Owen. Mr. Nesbit of Altoona offered four resolutions on the abuse of the freedmen, citizenship, loyalty and the treatment of colored soldiers. Mr. Price of Harrisburg, on colored men who refuse to accommodate persons of their own color in their business places. Mr. Geo. B. White of Philadelphia offered a resolution for one representative from each district League in Philadelphia on the Executive Board. Mr. Solicitor Bustill of Philadelphia requested lists of churches, lodges and associations with P.O. addresses. Nominating committee (one per county, on Mr. Bustill's motion): Daniel Williams of Blair Co., Geo. B. White of Phila. Co., Samuel Molson of Mifflin Co., O. L. C. Hughes of Dauphin Co., Aaron L. Still of Berks Co., Benjamin Wilson of Luzerne Co., Henry T. Busley of Erie Co., Benj. Fulpress of Allegheny Co., Franklin Johnson of Centre Co., Charles W. Nighten of Lawrence Co., John G. Chaplin of Huntingdon Co., Chas. H. Kelly of Lycoming Co. Business Committee chairman Prof. Vashon of Pittsburgh; on motion of Rev. Jos. A. Nelson of Phila. the report was taken up by resolutions. Resolutions adopted include: approval of retaining colored troops; protest to the Secretary of War and Lt. Gen. Grant at cruel treatment of colored soldiers in Texas; instruct the representatives to the National Equal Rights' League to urge reduction of the fifty dollar fee; commend the constitution of the Agricultural, Commercial, Literary, and Beneficial Society of West Philadelphia; any member who refuses to accommodate colored men in his place of business guilty of dereliction; accept the plan of the National Equal Rights' League. Afternoon session, Vice President Nesbit in the chair; prayer by Rev. Jos. A. Nelson. Executive Board to raise $5000 before March 4 next and to appoint assessors for each district, who are to supervise their districts and take note of all cases where colored men are assaulted on the public highways or thrust from rail road cars, and to prosecute such cases in the courts. (To be continued.) Non-Philadelphia names are in the text only.

events.name: Funeral of Maurice Hall, Bethel Church
events.location: from No. 1043 Lombard street to Bethel Church (Sixth St.); burial Lebanon Cemetery
events.description: Monday Nov. 13, 1865, 10 a.m., from Hall's residence, No. 1043 Lombard street. Cortege: official members of Bethel Church; Rev. Wm. Moore, pastor; the invited clergy; relatives; a vast concourse of friends. Route: up Eleventh street to Spruce, down Spruce to Sixth, thence to the church (11 o'clock). The choir chanted the dirge 'Why do we mourn departed friends'. Rev. R. F. Gibbs of Union Church read the 12th chapter of Ecclesiastes; prayer by Rev. Jacob Mitchell [VERIFY] of Wesley Church; sermon by Rev. Wm. Moore from Rev. 14:13. By request of brother Hall, Revs. S. Smith and Jos. Frisby [VERIFY] assisted; Smith made remarks, followed by Rev. Frisby. The Daughters of Conference and the Dorcas Society of Bethel Church were largely represented, as well as the Aged Home, a delegation from the latter headed by the matron; Maurice Hall was the leading spirit in the establishment of the Aged Home. At 12 1/2 o'clock his remains were borne to Lebanon cemetery. Funeral procession: relevant to the parades topic.

events.name: Harrisburg celebration and procession for the colored soldiers of Pennsylvania
events.location: Harrisburg, Pa.: State street, residence of Simon Cameron, Capitol grounds, Soldier's Rest; evening meetings at the Wesleyan Union Church and the Court House
events.description: Tuesday Nov. 14, 1865. Military and civic societies assembled on State street at 9 o'clock; line in motion by 10. Order of procession: Chief Marshal; Aids; Drum Corps of the 24th U.S.C.T.; Military, with arms; carriage drawn by four horses containing the Orator of the Day, Wm. H. Day, A.M.; carriage containing Presidents of several Equal Rights Leagues; carriages containing other officers; Delmonico Band; Paxton Lodge of Masons, in full regalia; colored citizens on foot. Owing to some misunderstanding a number of troops at Philadelphia were detained until too late to reach Harrisburg to form part of the procession. The procession halted before the residence of Hon. Simon Cameron, who spoke; calls for General Kiddoo, who acknowledged the compliment. At the Capitol grounds T. Morris Chester introduced Rev. J. Walker Jackson, who prayed; music 'America' by the band; Chester introduced as President Rev. Stephen Smith; Dr. J. H. Smith read resolutions (thanks to the colored soldiers; appeal to undo the 1838 constitutional amendment that deprived colored freemen of Pennsylvania of the franchise; opposition to colonization), which were adopted. Band played 'Tramp, tramp'; Prof. Wm. Howard Day of New York delivered the address. Procession re-formed and marched to the Soldier's Rest for a free dinner. Evening public meetings under the auspices of the State Equal Rights League: at the Court House, Dr. Smith, Mr. Matthews of Baltimore and Prof. Day; at the Wesleyan Union Church, Messrs. J. C. White, Jr., and O. V. Catto. No interference reported. Marshals are not named.

events.description: Conclusion of the proceedings. Committee of the whole with Mr. J. C. Bustill of Phila. in the chair. Mrs. Henry of Birmingham and Mr. R. Bell of Reading elected corresponding members. Business Committee (chairman Prof. George B. Vashon) resolutions adopted: an agent at Washington; unity of organizations, 'especially the secret institutions'; associations among the youth on the penny-a-week system; distribution of the Proceedings of the February Harrisburg convention held by the Executive Board at Philadelphia; mourning for Abraham Lincoln. Evening session Aug. 10, 8 o'clock, President Peck in the chair: Mr. Bustill reported the resolution taxing auxiliary leagues fifteen cents per member to defray the expenses of representatives to the National Equal Rights League; representatives appointed Mr. Wm. D. Forten of Phila. and Prof. Geo. B. Vashon of Pittsburgh; 500 copies of the proceedings to be printed; on motion of Mr. Fauset of Philadelphia the Christian Recorder adopted as the League's medium of communication; speakers Prof. Vashon and Bishop Wayman, singing by Mr. De Grath [VERIFY], a soldier of the U.S. Army.
